faceScanPage.summaryAttention: Several areas stood out this time — here's where to focus.

pores.name: Pores
tips: Niacinamide helps regulate oil and refine the look of pores over time
A gentle BHA toner 2–3x/week keeps pores from clogging
Daily SPF slows the collagen loss that stretches pores

blackheads.name: Blackheads
tips: Double cleanse in the evening to fully remove sunscreen and oil
A BHA (salicylic acid) toner helps dissolve buildup inside pores
Avoid harsh scrubbing — it can irritate skin without actually clearing pores

texture.name: Texture
tips: A gentle AHA 1–2x/week smooths texture without over-stripping
Layering hydration (hyaluronic acid) plumps and softens rough patches
Consistency matters more than intensity — little and often beats occasional harsh treatments

oiliness.name: Oiliness
tips: Niacinamide helps regulate sebum without over-drying
Don't skip moisturizer — stripped skin often overproduces oil to compensate
A lightweight gel moisturizer keeps oil balanced without heaviness

dryness.name: Dryness
tips: Ceramides help rebuild the skin's natural moisture barrier
Layer hyaluronic acid on damp skin, then seal it in with a moisturizer
Cut back on strong actives (retinol, AHA/BHA) until the barrier recovers

redness.name: Redness
causes: Too many actives layered at once
tips: Centella asiatica (cica) is one of the most consistently soothing ingredients for visible redness
Simplify your routine temporarily while skin recalms
Patch-test new actives on your inner arm before applying to the face

sensitivity.name: Sensitivity
tips: Prioritize a ceramide-rich moisturizer to rebuild the barrier before reintroducing actives
Avoid layering multiple actives (retinol + AHA/BHA) until skin calms down
Look for fragrance-free formulas while your barrier recovers

spots.name: Dark spots
tips: Vitamin C in the morning helps fade spots and protects against new ones forming
Daily SPF is the single most effective way to stop spots from getting darker
Niacinamide can help even out tone alongside a brightening active

acne.name: Active blemishes
causes: Excess oil combined with clogged pores
tips: A BHA (salicylic acid) toner helps clear congestion inside the pore
Benzoyl peroxide spot-treats active, inflamed blemishes
Avoid picking — it prolongs healing and increases the odds of scarring

acneScars.name: Post-acne marks
causes: Slow cell turnover leaving marks visible longer
tips: Niacinamide and vitamin C both help fade lingering discoloration
Gentle, regular exfoliation (AHA) speeds up how fast marks fade
Consistent SPF prevents marks from darkening further in the sun

wrinkles.name: Fine lines & wrinkles
tips: Retinol is the best-studied ingredient for softening the look of fine lines over time
Peptides support skin firmness alongside retinol
Daily SPF is what actually slows new lines from forming

darkCircles.name: Under-eye circles
causes: Thin under-eye skin showing blood vessels
tips: A peptide eye cream can help with puffiness and the look of fine lines
Gently pat products in with your ring finger — never rub the eye area
Sleep and hydration have an outsized visible effect on this area specifically

radiance.name: Radiance
causes: Buildup of dull, dead skin cells
tips: Vitamin C brightens and adds visible glow with consistent use
Gentle exfoliation reveals fresher skin underneath
Radiance responds fast to hydration — don't skip your moisturizer step

niacinamide.name: Niacinamide
niacinamide.summary: Regulates sebum, soothes, strengthens the barrier.

vitamin_e.name: Vitamin E
vitamin_e.summary: Antioxidant, often paired with vitamin C.

spf.name: Sunscreen (SPF)
spf.summary: UV protection — the final morning step.

retinol_aha_bha.headline: High over-exfoliation risk
retinol_aha_bha.reason: Retinol and AHAs both speed up cell turnover: combined the same night, they multiply redness, sensitivity and peeling.
retinol_aha_bha.recommendation: Alternate nights (e.g. retinol Mon/Wed/Fri, AHA the other nights) instead of layering them.

retinol_bha.headline: High over-exfoliation risk
retinol_bha.reason: Same logic as with AHAs: BHA and retinol stack irritation on an already fragile skin barrier.
retinol_bha.recommendation: Give each its own evening, never both at once.

retinol_benzoyl.headline: Benzoyl peroxide deactivates retinol
retinol_benzoyl.reason: Benzoyl peroxide oxidizes retinol and significantly reduces its efficacy, on top of irritating skin if combined.
retinol_benzoyl.recommendation: Use benzoyl peroxide in the morning and keep retinol for the evening, spaced by a few hours — or alternate days.

vitc_retinol_timing.headline: Two powerful actives, two different moments
vitc_retinol_timing.reason: L-AA vitamin C is unstable at a pH close to active retinol; combining them can neutralize part of their efficacy and irritate skin.
vitc_retinol_timing.recommendation: Vitamin C in the morning (antioxidant + protection), retinol at night. Simple, effective, zero conflict.

aha_bha_together.headline: Stacking exfoliants
aha_bha_together.reason: Using two chemical exfoliants the same evening raises the risk of a damaged skin barrier, especially on sensitive skin.
aha_bha_together.recommendation: Pick one per evening, or reserve the combo for very tolerant skin starting at low frequency.

niacinamide_vitc_myth.headline: Myth: this combination is actually safe
niacinamide_vitc_myth.reason: The belief that niacinamide + vitamin C form an ineffective complex comes from old studies at very high temperatures, not representative of a real routine.
niacinamide_vitc_myth.recommendation: You can use them together without issue. If your skin reacts, this combination isn't the cause — look at concentration instead.

peptides_aha.headline: Acidic pH can deactivate some peptides
peptides_aha.reason: Many peptides work best at neutral pH; an acidic exfoliant applied right before can reduce their efficacy.
peptides_aha.recommendation: Apply peptides at another time (morning routine, or a layer after rinsing/neutralizing the pH).

spf_am_only.headline: Retinol increases photosensitivity
spf_am_only.reason: Retinol makes skin more sensitive to UV. Since it's an evening product, the real thing to manage is your SPF the next morning.
spf_am_only.recommendation: No same-evening application to manage — just make sure to apply SPF the morning after a retinol night.
